title: List All Views
description: Learn how to list all views in a SQL Server database using system catalog views.

data.text: To list all views in a SQL Server database, query the sys.views or sys.objects catalog view.

data.title: List all views using sys.views
data.content: Returns schema name and view name for all views in the database.
data.code:
SELECT
    OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(v.object_id) AS schema_name,
    v.name
FROM
    sys.views AS v;

data.title: List all views using sys.objects
data.code:
SELECT
    OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(o.object_id) AS schema_name,
    o.name
FROM
    sys.objects AS o
WHERE
    o.type = 'V';

data.text: You can create a stored procedure to list views with optional filtering by schema and view name:

data.title: usp_list_views stored procedure
data.content: Creates a stored procedure to list views with optional filters.
data.code:
CREATE PROC usp_list_views(
    @schema_name AS VARCHAR(MAX) = NULL,
    @view_name AS VARCHAR(MAX) = NULL
)
AS
SELECT
    OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(v.object_id) AS schema_name,
    v.name AS view_name
FROM
    sys.views AS v
WHERE
    (@schema_name IS NULL OR
    OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME(v.object_id) LIKE '%' + @schema_name + '%') AND
    (@view_name IS NULL OR
    v.name LIKE '%' + @view_name + '%');

data.title: List Views Key Points
points: Use sys.views to list all views in the database.
Use sys.objects with type = 'V' as an alternative approach.
OBJECT_SCHEMA_NAME() returns the schema of a view.
You can create a stored procedure for filtered view listing.
